speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. You mentioned experiencing sudden-onset vertigo; can you describe exactly what you were doing when the symptoms started and how long the spinning sensation lasts?

speaker: Patient
text: 59-year-old male. The patient presents to the emergency department with a sudden-onset sensation that the room is spinning, leading to several episodes of nausea and vomiting. The symptoms started as he was going to bed and lasted for approximately 3 minutes. He mentions that he has never experienced anything like this before and currently feels at his baseline.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Benign Paroxysmal Positional Vertigo (BPPV). Based on the sudden onset of vertigo while changing position (going to bed), the brief duration of approximately 3 minutes, and the absence of other neurological symptoms, this clinical picture strongly supports BPPV. No further questions or tests are required for this diagnosis.
